messages:
sre-lead: Heads-up: we're planning a controlled dry-run to enable the new SLO-enforcement toggle in us-west-1 this Thu 2026-06-03 02:00-02:20 UTC. Purpose: validate automatic burn-rate enforcement and admission rejects under simulated burst traffic before we flip it broadly.

tanya.prod: Quick Q - what does "SLO-enforcement" do in practice?

sre-lead: Short: when enabled, the admission controller will proactively reject/queue requests that would cause projected SLO burn > configured threshold. It should prevent large-scale degradations but may cause proportional 429s for offending routes. This run is a dry-run with simulated load; we'll start with canary traffic and synthetic bursts.

mark.oncall: Expected customer impact?

sre-lead: Minimal. We'll target 2% canary of hosted traffic first, run loadgen to push burn-rate high for 6m, observe rejection counts. If healthy, we'll 10% for 8m. Rejections will be synthetic-only flagged; we won't enable permanent enforcement unless metrics match safety gates. We'll post to #status if we see >1m visible impact.

lucas.ml: What are the safety gates and abort criteria?

sre-lead: Abort if any: sustained error-rate increase >0.5% absolute for 10m; or P99 delta >600ms sustained 10m; or synthetic rejection-rate >20% for production routes beyond canary. Also abort if admission queue grows >1500 for 5m.

deploy-bot: scheduled job created: job_id=slo-enforce-dryrun-1954321987, canary=2%

infra-bot: Capacity check: us-west-1 hosted pools show 17% spare capacity. Dedicated pools unaffected.

bench-bot: loadgen plan posted: 6m spike at 1200 qps per node against canary slice, then 4m steady at 600 qps. Command:
```
loadgen run --job slo-dryrun-1954321987 --region us-west-1 --qps 1200 --duration 360 --targets canary
```

tanya.prod: Will support need to respond to customer tickets?

status-bot: We'll only post a public status update if we hit abort or if customers see >5m continuous errors.

mark.oncall: Who is primary during window?

sre-lead: Mark will own pager channel, Tanya owns comms, Lucas watches model-fallback/admission heuristics, I'll coordinate rollout and runbook.

mark.oncall: Runbook snippet for quick toggle:
```
# turn on dry-run enforcement
kubectl -n inference patch cm admission-config -p '{"data":{"slo_enforcement_mode":"dry-run"}}'
# enable enforcement (non-dry-run)
kubectl -n inference patch cm admission-config -p '{"data":{"slo_enforcement_mode":"enforced"}}'
# rollback to off
kubectl -n inference patch cm admission-config -p '{"data":{"slo_enforcement_mode":"off"}}'
```

lucas.ml: Suggestion: add a header in rejected responses so SDKs can surface a clear message to clients during testing: X-Redwood-SLO-Reject: dry-run.

sre-lead: good call  we'll add that for visibility.

deploy-bot: Reminder scheduled: 30m before window.

mark.oncall: I'll be on watch 01:40 UTC and will post immediate abort if thresholds hit.

tanya.prod: I'll prep a short support script and a canned message in case customers call; won't publish unless abort.

sre-lead: final note: if any app team wants to opt their routes out of the canary, DM me before Wed 23:59 UTC. We'll collect observations and decide whether to roll to more regions. Posting runbook link and exact job ids 20m before start. :white_check_mark:
